summary: Completed the initial scenario-complete review of Schneider Electric SE after its July 30 upper-Bollinger and bullish-MACD entries and strengthened July 31 upper-band state. Schneider's July 30 H1 release provides a contemporaneous fundamental explanation: H1 revenue rose 14.0% organically, adjusted EBITA rose 22.1% organically to a 19.3% margin, free cash flow reached EUR 1.631 billion, Data Center & Networks demand rose triple-digit in Q2, and full-year guidance was upgraded. A mature-compounder earnings-multiple valuation gives EUR 190/240/330 bear/base/bull values, a EUR 250 probability-weighted value, -13.80796051663878822746365404% expected return, -10.35597038747909117059774053% confidence-adjusted expected return, and a EUR 192 buy-below price versus the EUR 290.04998779296875 mark. The deterministic assessment is Sell/Avoid, watch-tier and ineligible because expected and base returns, downside payoff, margin of safety, timing and relationship gates fail. No conviction strategy was created; exactly one dependent AI-infrastructure idea refresh was queued.

evidence.claim: Schneider Electric's July 30 H1 2026 release reports EUR 21.226 billion revenue, up 14.0% organically, EUR 4.093 billion adjusted EBITA at a 19.3% margin, EUR 2.488 billion net income, EUR 1.631 billion free cash flow, and EUR 4.79 adjusted EPS. Energy Management produced EUR 17.641 billion revenue and a 22.4% adjusted EBITA margin. Data Center & Networks demand rose triple-digit in Q2 and sales grew strong double-digit, led by prefabricated solutions, cooling and three-phase UPS. Net debt reached EUR 15.360 billion and trade working capital absorbed EUR 1.208 billion. Management upgraded 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 10-13% and organic adjusted EBITA growth to 14-19%.

Schneider Electric's FY2025 release reports EUR 40.152 billion revenue, EUR 7.520 billion adjusted EBITA at an 18.7% margin, EUR 4.635 billion free cash flow, EUR 8.59 adjusted EPS and EUR 13.721 billion year-end net debt. It reports sharply accelerating pure data-centre demand and strong uptake across electrical panels, UPS, racks, prefabricated solutions and liquid cooling, plus lifecycle commissioning, modernization and maintenance demand.
